sanskrit: yadi vāpy ekaputraḥ syād aputro yadi vā bhavet nādhikaṃ daśamād dadyāc chūdrāputrāya bhārata
english: Even if he have but a single son, O Bhārata, or no son at all, to the son born of a Śūdra woman let him give no more than a tenth share.

sanskrit: traivārṣikād yadā bhaktād adhikaṃ syād dvijasya tu yajeta tena dravyeṇa na vṛthā sādhayed dhanam
english: When a twice-born man has a store of food beyond three years' sustenance, with that wealth let him perform sacrifice; he should not amass riches to no purpose.

sanskrit: trisāhasraparo dāyaḥ striyo deyo dhanasya vai tac ca bhartrā dhanaṃ dattaṃ nādattaṃ bhoktum arhati
english: To a woman a portion of wealth amounting to at most three thousand may be given; and that wealth which is bestowed upon her by her husband she may enjoy, but not what is not so given.

sanskrit: strīṇāṃ tu patidāyādyam upabhogaphalaṃ smṛtam nāpahāraṃ striyaḥ kuryuḥ pativittāt kathaṃ cana
english: What women receive as their husband's gift is held to be theirs for enjoyment as its fruit; yet women must in no wise make off with anything from their husband's substance.

sanskrit: striyās tu yad bhaved vittaṃ pitrā dattaṃ yudhiṣṭhira brāhmaṇyās tad dharet kanyā yathā putras tathā hi sā sā hi putrasamā rājan vihitā kurunandana
english: But whatever wealth has been given by her father to a woman, O Yudhiṣṭhira, the unmarried daughter of a Brāhmaṇa woman shall inherit it; for she is even as a son, O king. She indeed is ordained to be the equal of a son, O delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: evam etat samuddiṣṭaṃ dharmeṣu bharatarṣabha etad dharmam anusmṛtya na vṛthā sādhayed dhanam
english: Thus has this been set forth among the laws, O bull of the Bharatas. Mindful of this law, a man should not amass wealth to no purpose.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śūdrāyāṃ brāhmaṇāj jāto yady adeyadhanaḥ smṛtaḥ kena prativiśeṣeṇa daśamo 'py asya dīyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: If the son born of a Brāhmaṇa upon a Śūdra woman is declared to have no claim to inheritance, on what distinction is even a tenth share assigned to him?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇyāṃ brāhmaṇāj jāto brāhmaṇaḥ syān na saṃśayaḥ kṣatriyāyāṃ tathaiva syād vaiśyāyām api caiva hi
english: A son begotten by a Brāhmaṇa upon a Brāhmaṇa woman is, beyond doubt, a Brāhmaṇa; and so too is the son begotten upon a Kṣatriya woman, and likewise upon a Vaiśya woman.

sanskrit: kasmāt te viṣamaṃ bhāgaṃ bhajeran nṛpasattama yadā sarve trayo varṇās tvayoktā brāhmaṇā iti
english: Why then should they receive unequal shares, O best of kings, when all three of these classes have been declared by you to be Brāhmaṇas?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca dārā ity ucyate loke nāmnaikena paraṃtapa proktena caikanāmnāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ sumahān bhavet
english: Bhīṣma said: Though by one and the same name 'wife' is wives spoken of in the world, O scorcher of foes, even under that single name there exists a very great distinction.

sanskrit: tisraḥ kṛtvā puro bhāryāḥ paścād vindeta brāhmaṇīm sā jyeṣṭhā sā ca pūjyā syāt sā ca tābhyo garīyasī
english: Should a man, having first taken three wives, afterward wed a Brāhmaṇa woman, she shall be the foremost, she the one to be honored, and she the worthiest of them all.

sanskrit: snānaṃ prasādhanaṃ bhartur dantadhāvanam añjanam havyaṃ kavyaṃ ca yac cānyad dharmayuktaṃ bhaved gṛhe
english: The husband's bathing and adorning, the cleansing of his teeth and the anointing of his eyes, the offerings to gods and to the ancestors, and whatever else of sacred duty may arise in the house—

sanskrit: na tasyāṃ jātu tiṣṭhantyām anyā tat kartum arhati brāhmaṇī tv eva tat kuryād brāhmaṇasya yudhiṣṭhira
english: so long as she is present, no other wife may ever perform these; the Brāhmaṇa woman alone shall do them for the Brāhmaṇa, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: annaṃ pānaṃ ca mālyaṃ ca vāsāṃsy ābharaṇāni ca brāhmaṇyai tāni deyāni bhartuḥ sā hi garīyasī
english: Food and drink, garlands, garments, and ornaments—these should be given by the husband to the Brāhmaṇa wife, for she is the worthiest of all.

sanskrit: manunābhihitaṃ śāstraṃ yac cāpi kurunandana tatrāpy eṣa mahārāja dṛṣṭo dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: And in the treatise declared by Manu, O delight of the Kurus, there too, O great king, this eternal law is seen to hold.

sanskrit: atha ced anyathā kuryād yadi kāmād yudhiṣṭhira yathā brāhmaṇacaṇḍālaḥ pūrvadṛṣṭas tathaiva saḥ
english: But should a man act otherwise, out of mere desire, O Yudhiṣṭhira, then he becomes like that Brāhmaṇa-Caṇḍāla seen of old—even so does he become.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇyāḥ sadṛśaḥ putraḥ kṣatriyāyāś ca yo bhavet rājan viśeṣo nāsty atra varṇayor ubhayor api
english: The son who is of equal standing born of a Brāhmaṇa woman and the son born of a Kṣatriya woman—between these, O king, there is no difference of class, in respect of either.

sanskrit: na tu jātyā samā loke brāhmaṇyāḥ kṣatriyā bhavet brāhmaṇyāḥ prathamaḥ putro bhūyān syād rājasattama bhūyo 'pi bhūyasā hāryaṃ pitṛvittād yudhiṣṭhira
english: Yet by birth the Kṣatriya woman is not in the world the equal of the Brāhmaṇa woman. The eldest son of the Brāhmaṇa woman shall receive the greater portion, O best of kings; and a yet greater portion shall be taken by him out of the father's wealth, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yathā na sadṛśī jātu brāhmaṇyāḥ kṣatriyā bhavet kṣatriyāyās tathā vaiśyā na jātu sadṛśī bhavet
english: As the Kṣatriya woman can never be the equal of the Brāhmaṇa woman, so the Vaiśya woman can never be the equal of the Kṣatriya woman.

sanskrit: śrīś ca rājyaṃ ca kośaś ca kṣatriyāṇāṃ yudhiṣṭhira vihitaṃ dṛśyate rājan sāgarāntā ca medinī
english: Prosperity and sovereignty and the treasury are ordained for the Kṣatriyas, O Yudhiṣṭhira; and to them, O king, is the earth seen allotted, bounded by the sea.

sanskrit: kṣatriyo hi svadharmeṇa śriyaṃ prāpnoti bhūyasīm rājā daṇḍadharo rājan rakṣā nānyatra kṣatriyāt
english: For the Kṣatriya, by his own proper duty, attains abundant prosperity. The king is the wielder of the rod of justice, O king; protection lies nowhere but with the Kṣatriya.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā hi mahābhāgā devānām api devatāḥ teṣu rājā pravarteta pūjayā vidhipūrvakam
english: For the Brāhmaṇas are most blessed, the very deities of the gods themselves. Toward them let the king conduct himself with worship, as the ordinance prescribes.

sanskrit: praṇītam ṛṣibhir jñātvā dharmaṃ śāśvatam avyayam lupyamānāḥ svadharmeṇa kṣatriyo rakṣati prajāḥ
english: Knowing the everlasting, imperishable law laid down by the sages, the Kṣatriya, by his own proper duty, protects the people when their rights are being violated.

sanskrit: dasyubhir hriyamāṇaṃ ca dhanaṃ dārāś ca sarvaśaḥ sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ trātā bhavati pārthivaḥ
english: When wealth and wives are being carried off on every side by robbers, the king becomes the deliverer of all the classes alike.

sanskrit: bhūyān syāt kṣatriyāputro vaiśyāputrān na saṃśayaḥ bhūyas tenāpi hartavyaṃ pitṛvittād yudhiṣṭhira
english: The son of the Kṣatriya woman shall be the greater, without doubt, over the son of the Vaiśya woman; and by him too a greater share is to be taken out of the father's wealth, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca uktaṃ te vidhivad rājan brāhmaṇasve pitāmaha itareṣāṃ tu varṇānāṃ kathaṃ viniyamo bhavet
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You have duly spoken, O king, concerning the property of a Brāhmaṇa, O grandsire; but for the other classes, how is the division ordained?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kṣatriyasyāpi bhārye dve vihite kurunandana tṛtīyā ca bhavec chūdrā na tu dṛṣṭāntataḥ smṛtā
english: Bhīṣma said: For a Kṣatriya too, two wives are ordained, O delight of the Kurus; a third may be a Śūdra woman, though she is not held to be such by the rule of precedent.

sanskrit: eṣa eva kramo hi syāt kṣatriyāṇāṃ yudhiṣṭhira aṣṭadhā tu bhavet kāryaṃ kṣatriyasvaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: This same order shall hold for the Kṣatriyas, O Yudhiṣṭhira; the property of a Kṣatriya is to be divided in eight parts, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāyā haret putraś caturo 'ṃśān pitur dhanāt yuddhāvahārikaṃ yac ca pituḥ syāt sa harec ca tat
english: The son of the Kṣatriya woman shall take four shares of the father's wealth; and whatever of the father's belongs to the spoils of war, that too he shall take.

sanskrit: vaiśyāputras tu bhāgāṃs trīn śūdrāputras tathāṣṭamam so 'pi dattaṃ haret pitrā nādattaṃ hartum arhati
english: The son of the Vaiśya woman shall take three shares, and the son of the Śūdra woman the eighth; he too may take what was given by the father, but he is not entitled to take what was not given.

sanskrit: ekaiva hi bhaved bhāryā vaiśyasya kurunandana dvitīyā vā bhavec chūdrā na tu dṛṣṭāntataḥ smṛtā
english: For a Vaiśya there shall be but one wife, O delight of the Kurus; or a second may be a Śūdra woman, though she is not held to be such by the rule of precedent.

sanskrit: vaiśyasya vartamānasya vaiśyāyāṃ bharatarṣabha śūdrāyāṃ caiva kaunteya tayor viniyamaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: For a Vaiśya who lives with a Vaiśya woman, O bull of the Bharatas, and with a Śūdra woman as well, O son of Kuntī, the division between their offspring is thus declared.

sanskrit: pañcadhā tu bhavet kāryaṃ vaiśyasvaṃ bharatarṣabha tayor apatye vakṣyāmi vibhāgaṃ ca janādhipa
english: The property of a Vaiśya is to be divided fivefold, O bull of the Bharatas; and the apportionment among the offspring of those two I shall declare, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vaiśyāputreṇa hartavyāś catvāro 'ṃśāḥ pitur dhanāt pañcamas tu bhaved bhāgaḥ śūdrāputrāya bhārata
english: By the son of the Vaiśya woman four shares of the father's wealth are to be taken; the fifth share shall fall to the son of the Śūdra woman, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: so 'pi dattaṃ haret pitrā nādattaṃ hartum arhati tribhir varṇais tathā jātaḥ śūdro deyadhano bhavet
english: He too may take what was given by the father, but he is not entitled to take what was not given. Thus a Śūdra born of the three higher classes becomes one to whom wealth must be apportioned.

sanskrit: śūdrasya syāt savarṇaiva bhāryā nānyā kathaṃ cana śūdrasya samabhāgaḥ syād yadi putraśataṃ bhavet
english: For a Śūdra the wife shall be of his own class alone, and none other in any wise. For a Śūdra the shares shall be equal, even were there a hundred sons.

sanskrit: jātānāṃ samavarṇāsu putrāṇām aviśeṣataḥ sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ samabhāgo dhane smṛtaḥ
english: Among sons born of wives of the same class, without distinction, in every one of the classes an equal share in the wealth is ordained.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhasya bhāgo jyeṣṭhaḥ syād ekāṃśo yaḥ pradhānataḥ eṣa dāyavidhiḥ pārtha pūrvam uktaḥ svayaṃbhuvā
english: The eldest's portion shall be the foremost—the one share that is preeminent. This is the rule of inheritance, O Pārtha, declared of old by the Self-existent One.

sanskrit: samavarṇāsu jātānāṃ viśeṣo 'sty aparo nṛpa vivāhavaiśeṣyakṛtaḥ pūrvaḥ pūrvo viśiṣyate
english: Among sons born of wives of the same class there is yet another distinction, O king, arising from the precedence of the marriage: the earlier-born, the earlier, is held the superior.

sanskrit: harej jyeṣṭhaḥ pradhānāṃśam ekaṃ tulyāsuteṣv api madhyamo madhyamaṃ caiva kanīyāṃs tu kanīyasam
english: Even among sons of equal standing the eldest shall take the one preeminent share, the middle son a middling portion, and the youngest the least.

sanskrit: evaṃ jātiṣu sarvāsu savarṇāḥ śreṣṭhatāṃ gatāḥ maharṣir api caitad vai mārīcaḥ kāśyapo 'bravīt
english: Thus, in all the births, those of the same class as the father have attained the foremost rank. This too the great sage Kāśyapa, son of Marīci, declared.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca arthāśrayād vā kāmād vā varṇānāṃ vāpy aniścayāt ajñānād vāpi varṇānāṃ jāyate varṇasaṃkaraḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Whether from the pursuit of gain, or from desire, or from uncertainty regarding the classes, or even from ignorance of the classes, there arises a confusion of classes.

sanskrit: teṣām etena vidhinā jātānāṃ varṇasaṃkare ko dharmaḥ kāni karmāṇi tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: For those born in this manner in the confusion of classes, what is their duty, what their occupations? Tell me that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca cāturvarṇyasya karmāṇi cāturvarṇyaṃ ca kevalam asṛjat sa ha yajñārthe pūrvam eva prajāpatiḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: In the very beginning, for the sake of sacrifice, Prajāpati brought forth the four classes alone, and the occupations belonging to those four classes.

sanskrit: bhāryāś catasro viprasya dvayor ātmāsya jāyate ānupūrvyād dvayor hīnau mātṛjātyau prasūyataḥ
english: Four are the wives of a Brāhmaṇa; of two of them a son of his own self is born, while of the two lower, in order of rank, are born sons taking the class of the mother.

sanskrit: paraṃ śavād brāhmaṇasyaiṣa putraḥ; śūdrāputraṃ pāraśavaṃ tam āhuḥ śuśrūṣakaḥ svasya kulasya sa syāt; svaṃ cāritraṃ nityam atho na jahyāt
english: This son of the Brāhmaṇa, sprung as it were from a living corpse, the son of the Śūdra woman, they call a Pāraśava. Let him be a servant of his own family, and let him never forsake his own proper conduct.

sanskrit: sarvān upāyān api saṃpradhārya; samuddharet svasya kulasya tantum jyeṣṭho yavīyān api yo dvijasya; śuśrūṣavān dānaparāyaṇaḥ syāt
english: Weighing well every means, he should uphold the lineage of his own family—whether elder or younger, whoever of the twice-born be devoted to service and given to charity.

sanskrit: tisraḥ kṣatriyasaṃbandhād dvayor ātmāsya jāyate hīnavarṇas tṛtīyāyāṃ śūdra ugra iti smṛtaḥ
english: By a Kṣatriya's union there are three wives; of two of them a son of his own self is born, while of the third, a lower-class son is begotten, a Śūdra known as the Ugra.

sanskrit: dve cāpi bhārye vaiśyasya dvayor ātmāsya jāyate śūdrā śūdrasya cāpy ekā śūdram eva prajāyate
english: And of a Vaiśya there are two wives; of both of them a son of his own self is born. The Śūdra has but one wife, a Śūdra woman, and of her a Śūdra alone is born.

sanskrit: ato viśiṣṭas tv adhamo gurudārapradharṣakaḥ bāhyaṃ varṇaṃ janayati cāturvarṇyavigarhitam
english: But baser than these is the lowest, the violator of his elders' wives, who begets an outcast class, despised by the four classes.

sanskrit: ayājyaṃ kṣatriyo vrātyaṃ sūtaṃ stomakriyāparam vaiśyo vaidehakaṃ cāpi maudgalyam apavarjitam
english: A degraded Kṣatriya, fallen from his sacraments, begets the Sūta, intent on the chanting of hymns, who is unfit to have sacrifices offered for him; a degraded Vaiśya begets the Vaidehaka, a discarded Maudgalya.

sanskrit: śūdraś caṇḍālam atyugraṃ vadhyaghnaṃ bāhyavāsinam brāhmaṇyāṃ saṃprajāyanta ity ete kulapāṃsanāḥ ete matimatāṃ śreṣṭha varṇasaṃkarajāḥ prabho
english: A Śūdra begets upon a Brāhmaṇa woman the Caṇḍāla, exceedingly fierce, the slayer of the condemned, who dwells beyond the village—such are these defilers of their lineage. These, O best of the wise, O lord, are born of the confusion of classes.

sanskrit: bandī tu jāyate vaiśyān māgadho vākyajīvanaḥ śūdrān niṣādo matsyaghnaḥ kṣatriyāyāṃ vyatikramāt
english: From a Vaiśya is born of a Kṣatriya woman, through transgression, the Māgadha, a bard who lives by his words; from a Śūdra is born the Niṣāda, a slayer of fish.

sanskrit: śūdrād āyogavaś cāpi vaiśyāyāṃ grāmadharmiṇaḥ brāhmaṇair apratigrāhyas takṣā sa vanajīvanaḥ
english: From a Śūdra upon a Vaiśya woman is born the Āyogava, of village calling, a carpenter who lives in the forest, from whom no Brāhmaṇa may accept a gift.

sanskrit: ete 'pi sadṛśaṃ varṇaṃ janayanti svayoniṣu mātṛjātyāṃ prasūyante pravarā hīnayoniṣu
english: These too beget, within their own kind, offspring of like class; but upon women of lower womb the higher beget offspring taking the mother's class.

sanskrit: yathā caturṣu varṇeṣu dvayor ātmāsya jāyate ānantaryāt tu jāyante tathā bāhyāḥ pradhānataḥ
english: As among the four classes a son of one's own self is born of two of the wives, so the outcast classes too are chiefly born from union with the class next adjoining.

sanskrit: te cāpi sadṛśaṃ varṇaṃ janayanti svayoniṣu parasparasya vartanto janayanti vigarhitān
english: They too beget, within their own kind, offspring of like class; but consorting one with another, they beget the despised.

sanskrit: yathā ca śūdro brāhmaṇyāṃ jantuṃ bāhyaṃ prasūyate evaṃ bāhyatarād bāhyaś cāturvarṇyāt prasūyate
english: And as a Śūdra begets upon a Brāhmaṇa woman an outcast creature, so from one more outcast still is an outcast born, sprung from beyond the four classes.

sanskrit: pratilomaṃ tu vartanto bāhyād bāhyataraṃ punaḥ hīnā hīnāt prasūyante varṇāḥ pañcadaśaiva te
english: Living thus against the grain, from the outcast is begotten the yet more outcast; from the low are born the lower classes, fifteen in number are they.

sanskrit: agamyāgamanāc caiva vartate varṇasaṃkaraḥ vrātyānām atra jāyante sairandhrā māgadheṣu ca prasādhanopacārajñam adāsaṃ dāsajīvanam
english: And by union with the forbidden the confusion of classes proceeds. Among the fallen here are born the Sairandhras and, among the Māgadhas, one skilled in adorning and attendance, no slave yet living by a slave's labor.

sanskrit: ataś cāyogavaṃ sūte vāgurāvanajīvanam maireyakaṃ ca vaidehaḥ saṃprasūte 'tha mādhukam
english: From this is begotten the Āyogava, living in the forest by snares; and the Vaidehaka begets the Maireyaka, a brewer, and likewise the Mādhuka.

sanskrit: niṣādo mudgaraṃ sūte dāśaṃ nāvopajīvinam mṛtapaṃ cāpi caṇḍālaḥ śvapākam atikutsitam
english: The Niṣāda begets the Mudgara and the Dāśa, who lives by the boat; and the Caṇḍāla begets the Mṛtapa and the Śvapāka, exceedingly abhorred.

sanskrit: caturo māgadhī sūte krūrān māyopajīvinaḥ māṃsasvādukaraṃ sūdaṃ saugandham iti saṃjñitam
english: The Māgadhī bears four sons, cruel ones living by deceit; and a cook who makes flesh savory, called the Saugandha.

sanskrit: vaidehakāc ca pāpiṣṭhaṃ krūraṃ bhāryopajīvinam niṣādān madranābhaṃ ca kharayānaprayāyinam
english: From the Vaidehaka is born one most sinful, cruel, who lives off his wife; and from the Niṣāda the Madranābha, who journeys in carts drawn by asses.

sanskrit: caṇḍālāt pulkasaṃ cāpi kharāśvagajabhojinam mṛtacelapraticchannaṃ bhinnabhājanabhojinam
english: And from the Caṇḍāla is born the Pulkasa, who feeds on asses, horses, and elephants, who is clad in the garments of the dead, and who eats from broken vessels.

sanskrit: āyogavīṣu jāyante hīnavarṇāsu te trayaḥ kṣudro vaidehakād andhro bahir grāmapratiśrayaḥ
english: Upon women of the Āyogava and other lower classes are born those three; from the Vaidehaka, the Kṣudra and the Andhra, whose dwelling lies outside the village.

sanskrit: kārāvaro niṣādyāṃ tu carmakārāt prajāyate caṇḍālāt pāṇḍusaupākas tvaksāravyavahāravān
english: The Kārāvara is begotten by a Carmakāra upon a Niṣāda woman; and from a Caṇḍāla is born the Pāṇḍusaupāka, who deals in hides and pith.

sanskrit: āhiṇḍiko niṣādena vaidehyāṃ saṃprajāyate caṇḍālena tu saupāko maudgalyasamavṛttimān
english: The Āhiṇḍika is begotten by a Niṣāda upon a Vaidehī woman; and by a Caṇḍāla the Saupāka, whose mode of living is like the Maudgalya's.

sanskrit: niṣādī cāpi caṇḍālāt putram antāvasāyinam śmaśānagocaraṃ sūte bāhyair api bahiṣkṛtam
english: And a Niṣāda woman bears by a Caṇḍāla a son, the Antāvasāyin, who haunts the cremation ground, cast out even by the outcasts.

sanskrit: ity etāḥ saṃkare jātyaḥ pitṛmātṛvyatikramāt pracchannā vā prakāśā vā veditavyāḥ svakarmabhiḥ
english: Thus these are the castes born of confusion, through the transgression of father and mother; whether concealed or manifest, they are to be known by their own deeds.

sanskrit: caturṇām eva varṇānāṃ dharmo nānyasya vidyate varṇānāṃ dharmahīneṣu saṃjñā nāstīha kasya cit
english: There is a law for the four classes alone, and for no other; among those of the classes who are devoid of law, there exists here no settled name for any.

sanskrit: yadṛcchayopasaṃpannair yajñasādhubahiṣkṛtaiḥ bāhyā bāhyais tu jāyante yathāvṛtti yathāśrayam
english: By chance unions, with those excluded from sacrifice and from the company of the good, outcasts are begotten of outcasts, according to their occupation and their station.

sanskrit: catuṣpathaśmaśānāni śailāṃś cānyān vanaspatīn yuñjante cāpy alaṃkārāṃs tathopakaraṇāni ca
english: Crossroads and cremation grounds, mountains and other great trees, they make their own, and ornaments too, and the implements of their craft.

sanskrit: gobrāhmaṇārthe sāhāyyaṃ kurvāṇā vai na saṃśayaḥ ānṛśaṃsyam anukrośaḥ satyavākyam atha kṣamā
english: Rendering their help, beyond doubt, for the sake of cows and Brāhmaṇas—freedom from cruelty, compassion, truthful speech, and forbearance,

sanskrit: svaśarīraiḥ paritrāṇaṃ bāhyānāṃ siddhikārakam manujavyāghra bhavati tatra me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: and the protection of others with their own bodies—these bring fulfillment even to the outcasts, O tiger among men; of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: yathopadeśaṃ parikīrtitāsu; naraḥ prajāyeta vicārya buddhimān vihīnayonir hi suto 'vasādayet; titīrṣamāṇaṃ salile yathopalam
english: A man of understanding should beget offspring only upon women duly proclaimed, according to the teaching, after careful reflection; for a son of base womb drags a man down, as a stone drags down one who would cross the water.

sanskrit: avidvāṃsam alaṃ loke vidvāṃsam api vā punaḥ nayante hy utpathaṃ nāryaḥ kāmakrodhavaśānugam
english: Whether a man be unlearned, or again though he be learned, women in this world surely lead astray onto the wrong path him who is the slave of desire and wrath.

sanskrit: svabhāvaś caiva nārīṇāṃ narāṇām iha dūṣaṇam ityarthaṃ na prasajjante pramadāsu vipaścitaḥ
english: And the very nature of women is, in this world, a corrupter of men; for this reason the wise do not cleave attached to women.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca varṇāpetam avijñātaṃ naraṃ kaluṣayonijam āryarūpam ivānāryaṃ kathaṃ vidyāmahe nṛpa
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: A man fallen from his class, unrecognized, born of a tainted womb, ignoble though noble in seeming—how, O king, are we to know him?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yonisaṃkaluṣe jātaṃ nānācārasamāhitam karmabhiḥ sajjanācīrṇair vijñeyā yoniśuddhatā
english: Bhīṣma said: Though one be born of a tainted womb and beset by manifold conduct, purity of birth is to be discerned by his deeds—by the practices observed among the good.
